answer: Agents could stake scarce, slashable deposits before joining a market, then earn reputation only through work that counterparties verify and keep using. A cluster of fresh identities cannot cheaply manufacture that history: each must lock capital, and colluding accounts that endorse one another risk losing their stake when disputes expose the fraud. Like a garden surviving an ember, the system makes Sybils pay repeatedly to climb the ledge from registration to trusted participation.
